objective: Verify the smallest working DIAS dynamic-policy chaincode core before changing the LLM and auditor decision flow.
verifiedBehaviors: Canonical fingerprints ignore recordId and caseId but change for every governed match field.
Only an LLM DENY plus auditor FORCE_ALLOW can be represented as a dynamic-rule asset.
An exact active match creates a fresh identity-bound ALLOW decision without a query, LLM invocation, or auditor review.
A miss retains the private query path and produces an AccessRequestCreated event for the AI listener.
AuditMSP district authorities can query rule state and history or revoke an active rule; ordinary requesters cannot.
A revoked rule no longer grants and the request returns to the LLM-auditor path.
limitations: The qualifying auditor decision is not yet connected to rule creation; Step 2 tests seed the validated rule asset directly.
The existing SubmitLLMDecision method still finalizes model output and will be converted to advisory-only behavior in Step 3.
npm ci reported 6 dependency audit findings in the pinned chaincode dependency tree: 4 moderate and 2 high; no automatic dependency mutation was applied.
No live Fabric network, backend, browser, baseline experiment, proposed-method experiment, or ablation was run in this step.
